claims.text: Bigrassmannians \(v_{r,s,t,n}\) satisfy \(1\le t\le r,s\le n\) and \(t>r+s-n\); their parameters are \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\), \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 187-235]

groundings.excerpt:
187: The bigrassmannian permutations (besides the identity) are indexed by integers $r,s,t$ such that
188: $1\leq t\leq r,s\leq n$ and $t>r+s-n$. Let $v_{r,s,t,n}\in S_n$ be the bigrassmannian permutation uniquely
189: characterized by having unique descent at $r$, $v^{-1}_{r,s,t,n}$ having descent at $s$ and $v_{r,s,t,n}(t)=s+1$.
190: In one-line notation, one explicitly has
191: \begin{multline}\nonumber
192: v_{r,s,t,n}=1,2,\ldots,t-1,\ s+1,s+2,\ldots,s+r-t+1,\\
193: t,t+1,\ldots,s, \
194: s+r-t+2,s+r-t+3,\ldots,n;
195: \end{multline}
196: see \cite[Lemma~4.1]{RWY}.
197: For each basic element of $S_n$, a bigrassmannian permutation
198: $v$, define the \emph{basic ideal} of $H^*(X)$ as
199: \[J_v\coloneqq \mathrm{Span}_\mathbb{Z}\left\{\sigma_u\mid u\geq v\right\}.\]
200: It is shown in \cite{RWY} that $I_w$ decomposes into basic ideals. Specifically,
201: \begin{equation}
202: \label{eqn:thedecompabc}
203: I_w=\sum_{v\in {\mathcal E}(w)} J_v,
204: \end{equation}
205: where ${\mathcal E}(w)$ is the set of $u \in S_n$ which are minimal in the Bruhat order among those not
206: below $w$. The set ${\mathcal E}(w)$ is referred to as the \emph{essential set}, and consists only of bigrassmannian permutations \cite[Theorem 1.1]{RWY}.
207: As explained in \cite[Section~3]{RWY}, the projection
208: \[X\to \mathrm{Gr}_{r,n}\]
209: onto the Grassmannian of $r$-planes in $\mathbb{C}^n$
210: induces a split-inclusion $H^*(\mathrm{Gr}_{r,n})\xhookrightarrow{\iota} H^*(X)$. Consequently (see \cite[Proposition 3.1]{RWY}), elements of $H^*(\mathrm{Gr}_{r,n})$ generate $J_v$ in $H^*(X)$ if and only if they generate the contraction $J_v\cap H^*(\mathrm{Gr}_{r,n})$ inside $H^*(\mathrm{Gr}_{r,n})$.
211: In particular, elements of $H^*(\mathrm{Gr}_{r,n})$ \emph{minimally} generate $J_v$ in $H^*(X)$ if and only if they \emph{minimally} generate $J_v\cap H^*(\mathrm{Gr}_{r,n})$ in $H^*(\mathrm{Gr}_{r,n})$. This allows one to study the generation of $J_v$ inside $H^*(\mathrm{Gr}_{r,n})$ instead of $H^*(X)$ without loss of generality, enabling the use of symmetric function theory.
212: %It is established in \cite[Section~3]{RWY} (see specifically Proposition~3.1 and Theorem~3.2) that, without loss, the ideals $J_v$ of $H^*(X)$ can be considered instead in the cohomology ring $H^*(\mathrm{Gr}_{r,n})$ of the Grassmannian of $r$-planes in $\mathbb{C}^n$. This allows one to study $J_v$ by working with symmetric functions.
213: Let $\Lambda=\Lambda(x_1,x_2,\ldots)$ be the ring of symmetric functions with integral coefficients. This space has a ${\mathbb Z}$-linear basis consisting of \emph{Schur functions} $s_{\lambda}$,
214: where $\lambda$ is an integer partition. Consider the ideal
215: \[I_{r,n-r} = \mathrm{Span}_\mathbb{Z}\left\{s_\lambda\mid \lambda\nsubseteq (n-r)^r \right\} \]
216: of $\Lambda$. Then one has the following standard presentation of the cohomology of Grassmannians:
217: \[H^*(\mathrm{Gr}_{r,n})\cong \Lambda/I_{r,n-r}. \]
218: We will use an overline to denote the projection $\Lambda\to\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}$. Specifically, we will write $\overline{\Lambda}$ as a shorthand for $\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}$. We will also distinguish between $s_{\lambda}\in \Lambda$, the usual Schur function, and $\overline{s}_{\lambda}$ for its image in $\overline{\Lambda}$.
219: We resolve the minimality conjecture \cite[Conjecture~4.10]{RWY} about the basic ideals $J_v$:
220: \begin{theorem}\label{thm:main}
221: Given a bigrassmannian permutation $v=v_{r,s,t,n}\in S_n$ let
222: \begin{align*}
223: i&\coloneqq s-t+1,\\
224: j&\coloneqq r-t+1,\\
225: a&\coloneqq \min(n-r-i,r-j),\\
226: b&\coloneqq \min(i,j).
227: \end{align*}
228: Then the basic ideal $J_v$, thought of as an ideal of $H^*(\mathrm{Gr}_{r,n})\cong \Lambda/I_{r,n-r}$, is minimally generated by
229: \begin{equation}
230: \label{eqn:minimallist}
231: \{\overline{s}_{\mu} \mid i^j\subseteq \mu \subseteq (i^j,b^a)\}.
232: \end{equation}
233: \end{theorem}
234: That (\ref{eqn:minimallist}) generates $J_v$ is \cite[Theorem 4.8]{RWY}. The conjectural part, which we prove,
235: is the minimality claim, that is, no generator can be removed without changing the ideal.

claims.text: A valid tuple requires \(n,r,i,j,a,b,N\ge1\), \(r<n\), \(a+j\le r\), \(a+i\le n-r\), \(b\le i,j\), and \(N\le ab\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 300-304]

Put \(q=n-r\) and \[ (r^\vee,s^\vee,t^\vee)=(q,n-s,q-s+t). \] Then \(1\le t^\vee\le r^\vee,s^\vee\le n\) and \[ t^\vee>r^\vee+s^\vee-n. \] Indeed, \(t^\vee=q-s+t\ge1\) follows from \(t>r+s-n\); \(t^\vee\le q=r^\vee\) follows from \(t\le s\); \(t^\vee\le n-s=s^\vee\) follows from \(t\le r\); and \[ t^\vee-(r^\vee+s^\vee-n)=t>0. \] The original inequalities also force \(r,s<n\), hence \(r^\vee,s^\vee\ge1\).
The conjugated parameters are \[ i^\vee=s^\vee-t^\vee+1=j,\qquad j^\vee=r^\vee-t^\vee+1=i, \] and consequently \[ a^\vee=\min(n-r^\vee-i^\vee,r^\vee-j^\vee) =\min(r-j,q-i)=a,\qquad b^\vee=b. \]

The original core and both family upper shapes lie in the \(q^r\) box: \[ i\le q,\quad j\le r,\quad i+a\le q,\quad j+a\le r,\quad b\le i,j. \] Here \(q-i=t^\vee-1\ge0\), \(r-j=t-1\ge0\), and the two inequalities involving \(a\) follow from \(a=\min(q-i,r-j)\). The transformed statements are exactly \[ j\le r,\quad i\le q,\quad j+a\le r,\quad i+a\le q,\quad b\le j,i, \] so the transformed lower family is contained in the \(r^q\) box.

Conjugation of partitions gives the exact family correspondence \[ \left\{\lambda:j^i\subseteq\lambda\subseteq(j^i,b^a)\right\}' = \left\{\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\right\}. \] This uses \(b\le i,j\); the transpose of the \(a\times b\) lower adjoinment is an \(a\)-wide right adjoinment in the first \(b\) rows.

If \(a\ge1\) and \(1\le N\le ab\), then both \[ (n,r,i,j,a,b,N),\qquad(n,r^\vee,j,i,a,b,N) \] are valid: positivity is clear, \(r^\vee=q<n\), and the transformed containment conditions are \[ a+i\le q=r^\vee,\qquad a+j\le r=n-r^\vee. \]

The \(a=0\) boundary is excluded from valid tuples, since validity requires \(a\ge1\). Moreover, \[ a=0\iff (q-i=0)\ \text{or}\ (r-j=0) \iff (i=q)\ \text{or}\ (j=r). \] Under parameter conjugation these alternatives interchange. In either case both \(b^a\) adjoinments are empty, so each relevant family is the singleton core; no condition \(1\le N\le ab=0\) can hold.
